subject: Mythology
title: The Avatars of Vishnu
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Avatars of Vishnu.

hook.text: Vishnu has taken ten different forms across history, evolving from a fish to a god to save the world each time.

buildup.text: His first avatar was Matsya the fish, who warned humanity of a great flood — similar to the Noah story.

discovery.text: Narasimha, half man and half lion, appeared to kill a demon who could not be slain by man, beast, or god alone.

twist.text: Some scholars see the avatars as a mythological version of evolution: fish, turtle, boar, then increasingly human forms.

climax.text: The Buddha is sometimes included as the ninth avatar, showing how Hinduism absorbed and honored other traditions.

punchline.text: One god, ten forms, and a pattern that mirrors evolution itself.

quiz.question: What is notable about the sequence of Vishnu's ten avatars?
options: Each avatar is more destructive than the last
They progress from simple life forms to complex ones, mirroring evolution
Each avatar ruled a different continent
